_comment: JIT TEMPORARY ACCESS POLICY CONFIGURATION (Phase 6). Configuration, not rules.
The PAP pushes this document into OPA at data.agentic_iam.config.jit, and
policies/jit/issuance.rego and policies/jit/use.rego read it. The split is the
same one Phase 5.5 drew for loan thresholds: what a bound MEANS is a security
rule a reviewer reads in Rego; what the numbers ARE is an operational setting
a security committee changes without touching a rule.
Nothing in Python reads these values. There is no `if ttl > x` anywhere in the
application -- the AEM carries a requested duration and OPA decides what to do
about it.
FAILING CLOSED: if this document is absent from the engine, issuance denies
with JIT_POLICY_UNCONFIGURED rather than falling through. An unconfigured
maximum TTL must never read as 'unlimited' -- that is the single most
dangerous way for a configuration document to go missing, and it is exactly
the failure Phase 5.5 closed for loan thresholds.
WHICH ACTIONS MAY BE MANDATED AT ALL. An allow-list, never a deny-list: an
action nobody has analysed for reuse is not eligible, which is the safe
direction for a list that will be added to over time.
`read` on credit_records is the Phase 6 demonstration: a risk agent doing a
loan assessment reads several customers' credit profiles in one piece of
work, and making it re-authorise identically five times is ceremony rather
than control. Every read is STILL decided by the PDP -- the mandate removes
nothing but the repeated issuance.
DELIBERATELY ABSENT: approve_loan, disburse_funds and override_decision.
These are the Phase 5.5 human-approval actions, and they are excluded from
JIT entirely. The reasoning is in the `excluded_actions` note below and it
is the most important security decision in this phase.
`read` on loan_applications joined in Phase 6 so the mandate's financial
ceiling (max_amount_inr below) has a live path. It is a READ, not an
approval: it carries an amount, so the ceiling is exercised on every use,
and it touches nothing in the dual-control boundary. An agent holding such
a mandate still cannot approve any loan, at any amount.
WHY approve_loan IS NOT JIT-ELIGIBLE, recorded here because a future
operator WILL be asked to add it and should be able to read the reasoning
before they do.
A mandate carries a human decision forward across several actions. For a
loan approval that is precisely the thing Phase 5.5 exists to prevent: one
officer's approval covering a burst of loans would defeat maker-checker,
and a mandate issued while an amount sat in the single-approver band could
be spent on an application that has since moved into the dual-control band.
The amount band IS re-evaluated on every use, so the second failure is
caught -- but the first is not a policy question, it is a question about
what an approval MEANT, and a human who approved one loan did not approve
five. Excluding the action is the honest answer; relying on the band check
would be trusting a backstop to carry a decision nobody made.
If this is ever revisited, the mandate must be scoped to explicit
resource_ids and carry a max_amount_inr ceiling at or below the
single-approver limit, and the approval must have been given for that
exact set. Until that is designed and tested, the answer is no.
PHASE 7 ADDS `execute_payment`, for the same reason and with the same
force as approve_loan. A mandate carries an authorization forward across
several actions; a human who approved one payment did not approve five,
and a mandate issued while an instruction sat in the autonomous band
could be spent on one that has since moved into the dual-control band.
It is also absent from the allow-list above, so there are two
independent refusals.
A mandate with no resource_ids covers the resource TYPE and leaves
instances to policy. That is genuinely weaker than naming them, so it is a
configured choice rather than an accident of an empty list.
false here: for `read` on credit_records the per-use PDP evaluation already
checks the credential's allowedResources, so a type-scoped mandate cannot
reach a record the agent could not have read anyway. An action where that
is not true should set this true.
Whether a mandate may only be issued when a human approval already exists
and is valid.
false for the shipped eligible action, because `read` on credit_records is
not an escalated action -- it is permitted on the agent's own credential,
and requiring an approval to mandate something that needs no approval would
be ceremony. Any action that DOES escalate cannot be mandated without one:
issuance runs the full PDP evaluation, so a HUMAN_APPROVAL_REQUIRED verdict
refuses the mandate outright. That is structural, not configured.
A ceiling applied to any mandate over a resource that carries an amount.
Compared against the LIVE server-side attributes on every use, never
against a caller's claim. Set at the Phase 5.5 agent autonomous limit so a
mandate can never be used to act above what an agent could already do on
its own authority.
